analysis: Examined the shape-warmup addition: ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (new cells, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP env mode, bounded 20s budget, 500ms grace), ProviderLoop+ModelCalibration.swift:17-24 (shape warmup scheduled when calibration is not started), ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift:237 and 346-350 (new shapeWarmup dependency gated on cancellation, shutdown, drain and unloading), and StandaloneServer+StartupPreload.swift (startupShapeWarmup, scheduleShapeWarmups, retryShapeWarmups gated on running and not draining). The warmup uses synthetic token-count cells inside the provider process with no consumer prompt data. Cells are built from token counts rather than text, so no new plaintext exposure (A-001) and no logging of sensitive content is visible. The environment key is a local-operator knob that can only disable or force a bounded GPU workload, and the operator is already within TB-003 control. The warmup does not change attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), the coordinator wire contract, or the prefix-cache disk tier (T-041). Whether warmup requests donate to or populate the SSD prefix cache is not visible in the supplied files. Synthetic prompts could create cache artifacts or alter hit and miss timing. That depends on EngineV2Bridge.runShapeWarmupBeforeServing, startShapeWarmupIfNeeded and the engine's cache-salt handling, none of which were supplied. Also unverified are the preemption semantics versus real requests and the device-work admission and memory-floor checks. These bear on T-010, T-029 and T-041 availability and cache scope, so the next pass should inspect the bridge and engine implementation. The visible startup path is bounded by the existing registration gate timeout, and no concrete regression is identified here.
